rates_fed: Treasuries are pretty flat across the curve with no major moves on the day. There is no direct Fed commentary in today's update. The macro focus remains on geopolitical risk and energy supply rather than rate policy.
market_outlook: Adam's tone is cautiously neutral with a slight bullish lean into AI catalysts. The key catalyst to watch is Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote Wednesday night, followed by OpenAI's DevDay on September 29th and Micron earnings on September 30th — this cluster of AI events is the dominant near-term driver for the growth trade.
bull_case: AI-linked names are outperforming with broad strength across semiconductors and cloud infrastructure names as the market looks ahead to a dense slate of AI catalysts over the next ten days. Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of the Connect keynote, building bullish momentum. AutoZone's positive comp linearity commentary is lifting auto parts retailers, and housing names are also catching a bid. A potential Iran-Hormuz diplomatic resolution could ease energy market tension and provide a broader risk-on tailwind.
bear_case: Financials are broadly under pressure — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers are all underperforming, which is a notable drag on the equal-weight index and the Dow. CMS rate cuts for lab services hit Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp harder than anticipated, raising concerns about Medicare reimbursement risk across healthcare. Trump's approval rating has sunk to a career-low 32% per a new Reuters poll, adding political uncertainty ahead of midterms. SB Energy's IPO delay on valuation pushback signals that sentiment on the data center boom may be cooling at the margin.

company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point gross margin tailwind from tariff refunds and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit. Domestic comps came in at +1.6% versus the Street's +3.1%, though management noted positive comp linearity through the quarter. The opex ratio rose 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales.

MillerKnoll reported fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents, and crucially the beat holds up even excluding tariff refunds — stripping out the 11-cent tailwind still leaves EPS at 42 cents, well above consensus. Guidance is mixed with fiscal 2027 sales guidance trimmed but EPS outlook left unchanged. Stock is an earnings-linked outperformer on the day.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street at 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85% estimate. Revenue came in at $2.311 billion, down 8.4% year-over-year but slightly above the Street's $2.17 billion estimate. Management cited a difficult macro landscape as the primary headwind.

Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's Connect keynote Wednesday night at 7pm ET, and Shopify has agreed to allow Muse to complete purchases on its platform — a meaningful commerce integration win. Amazon has blocked Muse from its platform, creating a competitive divide. Investor expectations into the keynote are building and Meta shares are outperforming on the day.

Shopify will allow Meta's Muse personal AI agent to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform, positioning it as the preferred agentic commerce partner versus Amazon, which has blocked Muse. This is a meaningful distribution and monetization opportunity as agentic AI shopping scales. The partnership directly contrasts with Amazon's more closed approach.

Quest Diagnostics shares were hit Tuesday after CMS released new Medicare payment rates for lab services that represented a larger reduction than the market had anticipated. The cuts are pressuring the entire lab testing space. Both Quest and Lab Corp are underperforming meaningfully on the day.

Lab Corp shares fell alongside Quest Diagnostics after CMS announced Medicare lab service rate cuts that were steeper than expected. The broader managed care and lab testing sectors are both under pressure today. The rate cut magnitude caught the market off guard.

Cognex announced it will acquire RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. The deal expands Cognex's capabilities into the rapidly growing Physical AI and robotics segment. No earnings impact details were provided.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in the study. The results reinforce Viking's position as a credible competitor in the obesity drug space. The data is a meaningful positive catalyst for the stock.

On Holdings held its analyst day and outlined plans to achieve 2029 sales of at least CHF 5.6 billion versus the Street at CHF 5.4 billion, with EBITDA margins of 22% or better versus the Street's 21% estimate. The company also adopted a $1 billion share buyback authorization. Both the revenue and margin targets came in above consensus expectations.

tts_summary: Here's your midday read for Tuesday September 22nd. Markets are essentially treading water. The S&P 500 is flat, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Dow is off 43 basis points, and small caps are up 30 basis points. Treasuries are flat across the curve, Brent is just under a hundred dollars a barrel, and gold, silver, and bitcoin are all modestly lower. The big macro overhang is geopolitical. Investors are watching the United Nations for any signs of an Iran breakthrough — there are reports Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps to ease military pressure. Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline also appears to be coming back online at least partially, which is why crude is off a bit despite all the tension. On the domestic political front, Trump's approval rating has fallen to a career low of 32% in a new Reuters poll, down sharply even among Republicans, which is adding uncertainty ahead of the midterms. Now the bigger near-term story for active traders is the AI catalyst calendar. You've got Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote tomorrow night at seven Eastern, followed by OpenAI's DevDay on the 29th, and Micron earnings on the 30th. That's a dense ten-day stretch and it's driving real positioning today. Meta shares are outperforming, and it's not just the keynote hype — the Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads, and Shopify just announced it will allow Muse to complete purchases on its platform. That's a meaningful commerce win, especially as Amazon has chosen to block Muse. Shopify is threading the needle here as the open agentic commerce partner. On earnings, AutoZone beat the Street on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share at fifty-six dollars versus expectations of fifty-four, but the quality is questionable — the upside was entirely driven by tariff refunds and a non-cash inventory accounting benefit. Comps disappointed at plus 1.6% versus the expected plus 3.1%, though management flagged improving linearity. MillerKnoll was the cleaner beat — fiscal first quarter earnings per share of 53 cents against a 36 cent estimate, and even stripping out the tariff refund tailwind the company still would have beaten at 42 cents. Thor Industries missed on gross margins, which fell 230 basis points year-over-year, and management openly cited a difficult macro environment. Viking Therapeutics is getting attention after reporting 22% weight loss in its GLP-1 trial for VK2735 — a strong result that keeps them firmly in the obesity drug race. On the negative side, Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp are both getting hit hard after CMS released Medicare lab service rate cuts that were steeper than the market expected. Financials broadly are underperforming — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers are all in the red. Aerospace and defense is also weak. Directionally, the session feels like a coiled spring into the AI event calendar. Bulls want to see the Meta keynote deliver and for the Iran situation to de-escalate. Bears will point to financial sector weakness, cooling data center sentiment — SB Energy just delayed its IPO on valuation pushback — and the low-quality nature of today's earnings beats. Stay close to the tape into tomorrow night.
